narr: A surge of tropical moisture, combined with a an upper level low centered over an area near state borders of Arizona, Nevada and California is producing moderate rainfall over|central and northern Arizona.
ev: Highway 191 was closed due to flooding over the highway at Mile Post 491.8 between Round Rock and Rock Point (by Whale Rock) at 1135 PM. A social media video post showed a dangerous swollen wash along Highway 191.

The East Verde River near Childs (Gauge EVDA3) rose from 10 to 12.4 feet in less than 30 minutes at 930 AM on September 1. It dropped below 12 feet about 3 hours later. At 830 PM, it rose to 13.8 feet. The water dropped back to around 11.6 feet by 900 AM on September 2.

Heavy rain over the Little Colorado River Basin and tributaries created a surge of water at the river gauge (LCCA3) on the Little Colorado River near Cameron. The water rose from 1.8 feet to 5.43 feet on the gauge in less than 15 minutes at 1245 AM on 2 September. The water was still above 4.7 feet at 945 AM.

The stream gauge on Moenkopi Wash near Tuba City rose from 17.6 feet to 20.8 feet in less than half an hour at 430 PM on 1 September. The gauge went down to 18.4 feet then rose again to 23.7 feet in less than half an hour at 900 PM on 1 September. The water rose a third time to 22 feet in less than half a hour at 3:00 AM on 2 September. The water receded below 18 feet by 800 AM on 2 September.
Carrizo Creek near Carrizo (CRZA3) rose from 1 to 3.7 feet in less than an hour. The water dropped back below 2 feet about 3 hours later.
Heavy rain flooded a wash which created a waterfall over the rim and into Glen Canyon just below/south of Glen Canyon Dam.
Water was flowing over a 40 foot section of Highway 87 at Mile Post 343 near Coyote Wash.
